method: Direct 2022 national all-mode NAICS estimates. National all-mode total denominators from unchanged A01/A18/A19. Do not sum parent-child NAICS or combine A18 and A19; calculate no within-sector for-hire fractions until individual raw rows, flags and CV are verified.

analysis_profiles.question: Among consenting manufacturers, what share of third-party freight spend is actual LTL paid invoices, and which charge families have independently adjudicated errors?
analysis_profiles.counterargument: CFS high goods value may reflect valuable products, own-account trucking, truckload modes or multi-stage shipments rather than addressable LTL freight bills.
analysis_profiles.disproof: A rights-cleared representative paid-invoice sample shows no material LTL invoice volume, low bill complexity, or almost no correctly confirmed recoverable errors.

analysis_profiles.question: Do wholesaler accounts actually pay third-party LTL invoices with enough contract/accessorial variation to justify a second-look recovery workflow?
analysis_profiles.counterargument: Wholesale goods are often reshipped from manufacturers; summing CFS goods values or converting them to audit fees double-counts cargo and invents transport spending.
analysis_profiles.disproof: A stratified invoice study finds most movements parcel/TL/company-owned, few paid LTL bills or limited recoverable invoice variance.

analysis_profiles.question: Which warehouse operators are the legal freight-payable buyer rather than a third-party handler, and what is their directly paid LTL invoice exposure?
analysis_profiles.counterargument: Storage/fulfillment businesses may handle shipments without being the shipper of record or liable for transportation charges; high shipment value does not make them buyers.
analysis_profiles.disproof: Documented authority mapping shows most operators do not own carrier payment, cannot share invoices or have no applicable LTL bills.

independent_evidence_gaps.description: Verify national A18/A19 totals, survey year and original observed ZIP hashes
independent_evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Unchanged 2022 CFS original rows with national geography and mode identities; browser source hashes and a future separate local raw ZIP replay

independent_evidence_gaps.description: Measure industry-specific for-hire trucking instead of assuming all trucks are LTL
independent_evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Direct national NAICS 31-33/42/4931 x DMODE 111 rows with total SHIPDIST 001 and SHIPWT 01, all VAL/TON/CV flags checked

independent_evidence_gaps.description: Compare shipment distance and weight after checking additive strata and suppression
independent_evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Mode 111 per-industry SHIPDIST 02-10 / SHIPWT 02-10 with independent totals, CV flags, nonoverlap, rounding tolerance and denominator matching

independent_evidence_gaps.description: Determine actual paid LTL invoice incidence and contractual authority
independent_evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Human-authorized invoices matched to shipment, carrier, customer contract, payment, historical tariff and an independent adjudicator

recommended_source_action: Prepare read-only authorized, original-SHA-pinned extraction of direct NAICS x DMODE 111 total SHIPDIST and SHIPWT rows; keep uncertain/suppressed values missing rather than converting to zero.
